verdict.root_cause: The failing mechanism is inside productcatalogservice, not cartservice. Frontend's client-side gRPC errors in the incident interval are all status 13 INTERNAL returned by ProductCatalogService, with detail text naming a deliberately enabled failure feature flag on that service [tr_e7f975aa47de]. The connection succeeded and the callee answered with an application-level error, so this is a wrong configuration value — a fault-injection/failure flag left on — and the wrongness of that value is what breaks the request. That produces exactly the partial, intermittent error pattern frontend shows: a 183x jump in span error ratio from a near-zero baseline, peaking near 12% and repeatedly returning to zero, with a single change point at ~17:09:45 [tr_4056f8558e66]. Cartservice, the triage seed, is a bystander: its own log stream shows uninterrupted normal cart handling through 17:32:50 with no errors, restarts, or cache-connection failures [tr_2fc9d5d0535e], and every change on it in the window is a balanced apply/revert pair with nothing active at onset [tr_c6e0ceabaa1a]. Checkoutservice and frontend alerted because they are callers of the failing catalog path; the errors propagated toward the caller.
verdict.reasoning: Only one dispatch names a mechanism rather than an absence: frontend's logs show gRPC status 13 INTERNAL sourced from productcatalogservice with explicit feature-flag detail, and the specialist ruled out network/DNS/pod-unreachable precisely because the callee answered at the application layer [tr_e7f975aa47de]. Frontend's metrics corroborate the shape and timing — a new, partial, intermittent error elevation with a change point at ~17:09:45, not a total outage and not chronic [tr_4056f8558e66]. The seed service is excluded on two independent axes: its logs show healthy continuous serving with no error-severity output [tr_2fc9d5d0535e], and its change log contains only paired apply/reverts, the last landing 1.3h before onset with no residual drift [tr_c6e0ceabaa1a]. Cartservice metrics contribute nothing either way — the series is empty in both incident and baseline windows, so it is a persistent instrumentation gap, not a traffic drop [tr_ff732ad332a2]. Checkoutservice has no changes on record in the queried window, so it is not self-inflicted there [tr_c67453ea0428]; as a caller of the catalog path its 17:31:15 alert follows from the same upstream failure. Classifying this as bad_config rather than bad_deploy is deliberate: no wrong artifact is implicated, the service is running and responding — it is responding with an injected error because a flag value says to.
open_questions: No dispatch ever touched productcatalogservice directly: its change history, logs, and metrics are entirely unexamined, so the feature flag is inferred only from the callee's error text as seen by frontend.
Which flag, who set it, and when it was set are unknown; the ~17:09:45 change point is from frontend metrics, not from any productcatalogservice change record.

Frontend emitted no log lines between 17:16:56 and 17:32:52 in the retained result [tr_e7f975aa47de], so there is no direct log evidence that the catalog failure was still the active mechanism at the 17:31 alert time — the metric elevation is the only bridge.

The 16:57 payment-path failure (gRPC Unavailable, connection refused to 172.18.0.15:50051) is a second, distinct failure mode whose source service was never identified or investigated; whether it recurred at 17:31 and drove checkoutservice's alert is unsettled.

Checkoutservice's change query was scoped to the seed at hops=0 and its window started at the incident timestamp rather than covering the hours before it [tr_c67453ea0428], so pre-onset changes to checkoutservice and to any of its callees remain uncovered.

Cartservice's span metrics are absent in both windows, so request rate, latency, and restart/readiness counts for the triage seed were never actually measured; the log-based exoneration rests on a truncated stream missing ~17:01:04-17:32:32.

The cadence of automated apply/revert fault-injection on cartservice roughly every 6h [tr_c6e0ceabaa1a] raises the question of whether the same automation targets productcatalogservice, which would make the catalog flag scheduled rather than accidental — and would change the remediation from a revert to disabling the schedule.

alternatives.root_cause: A payment-path dependency (the service at 172.18.0.15:50051) is down or refusing connections, failing checkout and surfacing as frontend charge-card errors.
alternatives.why_not: The only observation of this signature is at 16:57, before the frontend error-ratio change point at ~17:09:45, and the frontend specialist explicitly distinguished it from the later interval's errors, which name a different dependency and a different status [tr_e7f975aa47de, tr_4056f8558e66]. It remains live because checkoutservice alerted at 17:31:15 and nothing rules out recurrence in the unlogged 17:16:56-17:32 gap.

alternatives.root_cause: The 17:31 alerts have a cause distinct from the productcatalog flag, which was already active from ~17:09 and merely coincides with the alert window.
alternatives.why_not: The frontend error elevation is continuous from the ~17:09:45 change point through the window with no second change point [tr_4056f8558e66], so one mechanism accounts for the whole interval; positing a second requires evidence no dispatch produced. Checkoutservice also has no changes on record in the covered window [tr_c67453ea0428].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. The obvious candidate — revert_config on productcatalogservice — fails its own first precondition: no prior configuration for productcatalogservice is recorded in any evidence on this board. Its change history was never queried at all; the failure feature flag is known only from detail text inside a gRPC status 13 returned to frontend between 17:16:51 and 17:16:56 [tr_e7f975aa47de], and the ~17:09:45 change point is a frontend metric artifact, not a productcatalogservice change record [tr_4056f8558e66]. A revert needs a prior value to restore, and this system has not observed one. The unblocking step is a change_history query on productcatalogservice covering at least the six hours before 17:09:45; if it returns a flag being set to an enabled value with a recorded prior value, revert_config on productcatalogservice becomes proposable and its effect would be measurable as frontend's span error ratio returning from its ~2.5% incident mean to the ~0.014% baseline within two 2m rate windows.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if productcatalogservice's change history does contain a recorded prior configuration and a flag change landing near 17:09:45 — in which case the delay cost real error minutes and revert_config should have been proposed immediately. It is also wrong in the other direction if the cadence in [tr_c6e0ceabaa1a] — balanced apply/revert pairs on roughly a 6h schedule, all attributed to platform-automation — extends to productcatalogservice, because then a manual revert would be re-applied by the next scheduled cycle and the correct fix is disabling the schedule, which is outside this system's permitted actions entirely. Note also that frontend emitted no log lines between 17:16:56 and 17:32:52 [tr_e7f975aa47de], so no observation currently confirms the catalog flag was still the live mechanism at the 17:31 alert; if the flag self-reverted on schedule before 17:31, any revert would be acting on an already-healed system and its apparent success would be misattributed.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is prolonged partial failure: frontend continues returning errors on roughly one in ten calls at peak, and checkoutservice callers keep alerting, for as long as it takes to query productcatalogservice's change history. The risk avoided is larger. Had revert_config been fired at productcatalogservice on this evidence, a container recreate with no recorded prior configuration could restore a stale or empty environment — including dependency addresses — and convert an intermittent 12% application-level error into a hard outage of the catalog path. That path is what every product-listing and cart-add request traverses. Separately, the 16:57 payment-path failure (gRPC Unavailable, connection refused to 172.18.0.15:50051) is an unattributed second mechanism [tr_e7f975aa47de]; if it, not the catalog flag, drove the 17:31 checkoutservice alert, then any catalog action leaves the actual fault untouched while consuming the incident's attention.
proposal.blast_radius: The abstention itself changes nothing and is seen by nobody. The action it declines to take would have hit productcatalogservice, whose inbound caller named in this incident is frontend, with checkoutservice and loadgenerator downstream of frontend's failures; those three would have seen connection resets for the duration of the container recreate. cartservice, adservice, recommendationservice, currencyservice, emailservice, paymentservice, shippingservice, and accountingservice are untouched either way.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting simultaneously across cart, frontend, and checkout paths is a multi-service event, not a single quiet warning, so it cannot be dismissed. The shared cart/checkout fan-in suggests a downstream dependency, but no evidence exists yet.
